chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'Is there a known time for the Zakat to be given during it?' So he said: 'That differs based on when the man attains the wealth; and as for Al-Fitra, its time is known.'

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Al-Fitra (the fixed alms given at the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in timing between Zakat and Fitrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the variable timing of Zakat, which is contingent upon the actual acquisition of wealth (nisab), and the fixed, lunar-calendar-based timing of Fitrah. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential principle that Zakat is a tax on accumulated wealth triggered by specific conditions, whereas Fitrah is a ritual obligation tied to the month of Ramadan. The narration underscores the flexibility in Zakat collection to accommodate different economic realities, contrasting it with the uniformity of the charitable pre-prayer offering.
